what: Fabrinet assembles optical and electronic products for other companies. Its factories in Thailand build the transceivers that move data by light inside data centres, laser modules and automotive sensors.
customers: Networking and optical equipment companies, who design the products and have Fabrinet build them.
money: transceivers and optical modules for data centres and telecom
automotive sensors, lasers and industrial electronics
moat: Precision optical assembly needs clean rooms, trained technicians and process control that take years to build. Customers qualify a line and leave it there.
risks: Revenue is concentrated in a few large customers, principally Nvidia and Cisco
Free cash flow was negative by $191M as it funded inventory and new capacity for the AI ramp
Contract manufacturing earns a thin margin and customers can move volumes
opportunities: Revenue grew from $2.3B to $4.6B in four years, and is $5.1B over the last twelve months
Analysts see about 81% upside, with 9 covering the stock
$875M of cash against $4M of debt, so the capacity expansion is self-funded
watch: Optical communications revenue and the share coming from data centre customers.
